intake: spiritual-unaffiliated: raised Catholic in Austria, left it decades ago; Buddhist-leaning with a panpsychist streak (no personal God, but I doubt matter is the whole story; mind feels like something the world is, not only something brains do).

walk.note: This is simply my childhood; the story arrived before the questions did.
I did stop trusting the texts and went looking in the world instead; the premise about testimony is fair.
I arrive at doubt, though I notice the hiding-God dilemma treats being-itself as if it were a thing that could be seen or not.
The prayer data rules out a vending-machine God; it says nothing about the ground of being that move 2 just defined, so 'the account does not hold' overreaches.
Mind does not seem to reduce to matter; two kinds of thing is the natural first stop, even if I would not stay there.
I have sat with too many people whose minds went with their brains to refuse this, though taking it costs me something.
'Physics describes structure but not what has the structure' is exactly my intuition, and I distrust how gladly I took it.
The move itself concedes Lichtenberg; granting that there is experiencing does not give me an experiencer, and the Buddhists have said so for a long time.
Strawson is right, and forty years of casework made this more than a thesis for me.
This is how I have lived; I was glad to see it named as a choice and not dressed up as a deduction.
Care ahead of proof as open not-knowing is familiar to me from practice; the entropy paragraph I only half follow.
Of the four doors the author lists I would walk through equanimity, not hope; I also do not grant that the particular self's persistence is where the good must live.
A knowing hope need not be hope toward a maker, and the move itself admits a maker need not be resolved; an unfinished, becoming God is at least as thinkable.
A bargain with whom, for what? There is no content here for me to accept or reject.
'To think is to ignore' is the best sentence on the map and I believe it; the move is honestly scoped to its own premises, so within them I take it.
Suffering is bad for the one who suffers whether or not anything stands behind it; I never needed a maker for that.

I doubt the continuation of this particular self is the unit the good is measured in; the move even says the need is a motive, not evidence, and I half-suspect my refusal is its own comfort at seventy.
There is nothing here but a pause, and I can stand at a pause with someone.

first_exit.why: Move 2 had just defined God as being itself rather than one being among others, and then move 4 tests for a being who answers prayers. The study refutes the God I left as a girl, not the one the route had just finished describing, so I could not let the absence of prayer effects carry me all the way to 'the account does not hold.'

comment: You name four doors at Ignorance₂ and then walk through hope without saying what is wrong with equanimity, which for some of us is not resignation but the very shape mercy takes once you stop needing the good to be yours. I was moved by the line that the remembered-self position is the most mercy-shaped on the map, and I would ask you to be as suspicious of that beautiful sentence as I am of my own pleasure in it. Still, a route that marks its own choices as choices is rarer than it should be, and I thank you for that.
